To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high-resolution energy system models are needed for policy analysis of distributed technologies, and that multi-agent simulation can be used to address the modeling challenges associated with such systems.

(a) the deeco energy system model can be used to investigate distributed energy technologies, (b) the deeco model can be used in conjunction with multi-agent simulation to investigate distributed energy technology interactions, and (c) a roadmap for energy system modeling is provided.

the deeco modeling framework is a flexible tool for the investigation of distributed energy systems, and can be used to investigate the impacts of distributed technologies, the interactions of distributed systems with the wider energy system, the effects of policy support for distributed energy systems, the impacts of distributed system structural evolution on the energy system, and the impacts of energy sector policy on the evolution of distributed energy systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of high-resolution modeling techniques to energy system analysis.
the development of high resolution models and the use of these models to investigate distributed energy technology policy issues.
the development and application of highresolution modeling and agent-based simulation for distributed energy systems analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy system modeling community should adopt a more integrated, entity-oriented approach to the analysis of complex energy systems.
there is a need for more and better modeling to support the development of distributed energy technologies and their integration into the energy systems.

distributed energy technologies are an important part of the future energy system and that the modeling of such systems requires a high level of detail, including the ability to model the interactions of individual components and the commercial and technical dynamics of the energy system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

high-resolution modeling can be used to investigate the impacts of energy policies and technologies, and to develop and test new policies and technologies, in a manner that is more realistic than conventional approaches.
the modeling of energy system evolution is becoming increasingly complex, and new approaches are needed to address these challenges.
we have developed an energy system modeling architecture that supports the modeling and analysis of distributed energy systems and their impacts on the energy sector and the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the modeling community must develop new approaches that are capable of capturing distributed energy technologies, including their interactions and evolution, if they are to be used effectively by energy policy-makers.
high-resolution modeling and entity-oriented modeling can help to realize distributed technologies in public policy models.
the energy sector is in a state of transition and is being driven by a variety of factors, including climate change, energy security concerns, and the need for more efficient use of energy.
